subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue with only per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This choice defines a public security/config contract and default behavior for scheduled autonomous runs, including whether existing announce-mode jobs that directly use `message` keep working by default.

options.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence, docs, and tests for message-tool denial across delivery modes.

options.title: Inherit Subagent Policy
options.body: Apply `tools.subagents.tools` to cron sessions as well, reducing config surface while coupling two different execution modes.

options.title: Keep Per-Job Only
options.body: Avoid a new global cron policy and rely on `payload.toolsAllow`, docs, and delivery safeguards for scheduled runs.

recommendation.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence, docs, and tests for message-tool denial across delivery modes.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history in the current policy resolver and cron runtime surfaces that frame this decision.
